A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpanNorm work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including content moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original dense and MoE training experiments, benchmark evaluations, scaling studies, and representation and gradient analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds topology comparisons, a GQA experiment, and empirical measurements of pre-normalization signal statistics.

M1.justification: The SpanNorm residual connections, first-layer normalization, initialization strategy, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. GQA was already supported by the architecture described in v1; v2 adds an evaluation of that configuration.

E1.justification: Both versions use SlimPajama training data and the same language-modeling and downstream evaluation benchmarks. The added topology and GQA experiments change model configurations, not the represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated Parallel Transformer and ResiDual comparators in Table 4 at 5B parameters and 200B tokens. This substantially broadens comparison to alternative block topologies beyond the retained normalization baselines. LayerNorm Scale becoming LayerNorm Scaling is only a naming change.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 740M/30B-token GQA configuration with 24 query heads and 8 key-value heads, plus layer-wise measurement of attention and FFN pre-normalization standard deviations in the 64-layer 5B model. Existing benchmark protocols, training settings, and depth-scaling configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test alternative residual topologies, robustness to replacing MHA with GQA, and empirical support for the homogeneous-variance assumption (Section 6 and Appendix A.2). These materially expand the architectural and mechanistic checks. The 512-layer stress test is retained and relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Figure 14's three-seed gradient analysis and individual-run traces. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes. The new activation standard deviations describe internal signals, not uncertainty in benchmark performance.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports average accuracy of 66.6 for SpanNorm, 65.0 for Parallel Transformer, and 63.4 for ResiDual. Table 5 adds GQA averages of 51.8 versus 50.8 for PreNorm, although WinoGrande is lower at 52.1 versus 52.5. Table 6 adds signal statistics with FFN/attention standard-deviation ratios of 0.96–1.19. These are substantial added result sets; existing benchmark and width-scaling scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.1, Theorem 4.1, the gradient derivations, and the appendix proof remain mathematically unchanged. Appendix A.2 supplies empirical evidence for an existing assumption, not a new formal argument. The proof heading's theorem-number correction is editorial.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about reconciling stability and performance, avoiding representation collapse, scaling deep models, and preserving computational efficiency. The new experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 newly states that SpanNorm addresses dynamic training pathologies rather than static rank collapse at initialization, distinguishing its causal setting from prior bidirectional-attention analysis. V2 also interprets the new GQA and topology comparisons as evidence of attention compatibility and structural advantages, and the new signal measurements as support for Assumption 3.1.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new GQA head configuration and training budget, and identifies the model and signals used for the variance diagnostic. Existing optimizer settings, learning-rate schedules, data-processing information, and pseudocode are retained. The extreme-depth setup is relocated from Appendix D.1, not newly disclosed.

R1.justification: V2 adds Chowdhery et al. (2023), Xie et al. (2023), and Nait Saada et al. (2025), positioning SpanNorm against parallel/dual residual architectures and distinguishing training-time collapse from initialization-time rank collapse. The changed Mix-LN bibliography entry refers to the same work.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language and terminology edits, adds conference and conflict-of-interest text, consolidates the extreme-depth discussion in Section 6, and reorganizes Appendix A into proof and empirical-justification subsections. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 4–6 and moves the existing depth-scaling plot from appendix Figure 11 to main-text Figure 8. Other appendix displays are renumbered or repositioned, and Figure 13 is resized with an explicit 10^6 throughput multiplier. The existing plots and overall visual format are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added topology controls, GQA evaluation, and variance measurements strengthen support for the existing method, while Appendix C.2 clarifies an important applicability boundary. These are targeted improvements rather than a resolution of the paper's general theoretical claims: the proof is unchanged, and Table 6's finite-depth measurements provide limited support for the broader homogeneous-variance assumption.
